v0.15.0·Beta·MIT·Windows and macOS

Heavy CAD, made light enough for a browser.

MeshOptimiser opens a heavy CAD assembly, keeps one copy of every part that repeats, and gives you a small GLB plus a viewer to look around, clean up and export. It’s free, it’s open source, and nothing leaves your computer.

Download View on GitHub Read the docs

See what is inside

Pull it apart, and look inside.

This is a real mesh, a rear derailleur in 43 parts, and it comes apart as you scroll. In the app every pin, bolt and bushing has its own row, its own triangle count, and a button to hide it, simplify it or take it out.

320 MB → 11 MB
The README’s example: a STEP assembly down to a compressed GLB.
About 10× smaller
GLBs shrink that much with Meshopt compression, through gltfpack.
1 mesh, many positions
Identical parts are found at any rotation or position and drawn once.
10,000+ nodes
The part tree stays quick and searchable at that size.

Why

A tool for getting heavy CAD assemblies into the browser.

The problem is a practical one. A real STEP file can hold 400 identical bolts, 80 duplicate brackets and half a million broken triangles, and a browser is still expected to draw it. MeshOptimiser reads the assembly, spots the parts that are the same and keeps one mesh with a list of positions, rebuilds the bad geometry, and drops what’s too small to see.

What you get back is a compressed GLB and a viewer to look at it in: the part tree, recolouring, mesh tools, a library of parts to add, and export. It runs on your own machine with Python and a browser, as an open take on what tools like Pixyz do.

What the pipeline collapses
400 bolts × 50 KB→1 mesh × 50 KB + 400 positions
80 brackets × 12 KB→1 mesh × 12 KB + 80 positions
500K broken triangles→Rebuilt, and the tiny ones dropped
320 MB STEP→11 MB compressed GLB

How it works

Three steps from STEP to the browser.

  1. 01

    STEP in

    Drop a .step or .stp file on the start screen, or run the converter from the command line.

  2. 02

    Convert

    OpenCascade reads the whole assembly with its names and colours. Repeated parts become one mesh, surfaces are rebuilt, tiny parts are dropped and the result is compressed.

  3. 03

    GLB out

    Open it in the viewer to look around, recolour, reduce, tidy the tree and export.

In motion

Tools that do one job, and say what it saved.

All features

A closer look

Built for assemblies with thousands of parts.

01

One button, half the triangles

Smart optimise runs every clean-up the app has, in order: empty and broken parts, hidden parts, fasteners, tiny parts, holes in flat faces, and then a reduction to the target you set. On this gearbox it took 646,064 triangles down to 322,988 and showed what it had saved. One Ctrl+Z puts it all back.

02

Bolts, found by their shape

Names in a CAD export rarely say what a part is. Fasteners cuts each part across its axis and reads the outline: a round shank with a wider head, six flats around a hole, a flat ring. It finds hex bolts, socket screws, nuts and washers whatever they’re called, and leaves bushings, bearings and O-rings alone. Forty-eight here, 22,760 triangles.

03

72,666 triangles down to 212

Smart fit used to turn a bracket into a brick. Blocks rebuilds a part from a coarse grid, so its steps, arms and openings stay where they were. Here it took two heavy parts of a gearbox from 72,666 triangles to 212.

04

A bolt that brings its own nut

Tick it on, pick the nut and set how far from the head it sits. The nut is part of the bolt’s own shape, in the bolt’s thread. It’s one part in the tree and one undo step, and it can’t slide off the end.

Try it

Search is how you get around.

This is the app’s own search, filled with a rear derailleur’s parts. Type a part, a library item or a command. The arrow keys move, Enter runs, and it does sums too.

  • boltThe bolts in the scene and every bolt in the library, in one list.
  • 12*25.4Sums are worked out as you type. Enter copies the answer.
  • 2 inA length in inches comes back in millimetres, which is what the scene uses.
  • fillCommands are in the same list, with their shortcuts.
    ↑↓ choose↵ runEsc clear12*25.4 · 2 in · a part’s name

    Try it

    The commands come to you.

    This is the app’s own Quick wand, on three parts of a rear derailleur, drawn with the app’s shapes, icons and colours. Point at a slice and it lights up; a slice with a group fans its commands out; click one to run it. Click a part first and the ring changes to work on it.

    • PointPoint at a slice and it lights up. A slice that holds a group fans its commands out.
    • ClickClick a command to run it. Click a part first, and the ring changes to work on that part.
    • Hold WIn the app the ring opens round the pointer. Here it moves to it: let go on a slice to run it.
    • EscPuts the ring back in the middle and runs nothing.

    Latest release

    v0.15.0

    Full changelog

    The commands come to the pointer. Hold W and a ring of commands opens under it. The rest is about making a model lighter without breaking it: a repair, a way to remove the faces nobody sees, merging and selecting by rule, Untriangulate, a wireframe that shows polygons, and a simplifier that now looks after normals, UVs and colours.

    • NewQuick wand (hold W). A ring of commands opens round the pointer; move toward a slice and let go of W. Only the direction counts, so a short flick is enough. With a selection it has Hide, Reduce, Delete and More; with nothing selected it has Fit view, Select all, View, Show all, File and Clean. A slice that holds a group fans out when the pointer is on it (Decimate −25 % to −90 %, Smart fit, Split and Fill holes; the views; Save; the clean-ups). A command that cannot run stays on the ring, dimmed, and says why. A quick tap of W leaves the ring open to click; Esc, any other key, the wheel or a click outside closes it, and it never runs anything by accident. You can try it on the home page.
    • NewRepair mesh joins doubled vertices, removes empty and doubled triangles and turns faces so that neighbours agree which side is out. Remove hidden faces looks at each part from many sides and deletes the faces that never show: the inside of a housing, the faces where two parts press together. Both undo in one step.
    • NewMerge by material or by group joins parts into one mesh per material or per group. Select by rule picks parts by name, material, group, triangles and size, or by whether they are shown, flagged, instanced or selected, and says how many fit as you type.
    • NewUntriangulate turns neighbouring flat triangles into one polygon and cuts it again with the fewest triangles, without changing the shape: a flat plate of 200 triangles becomes 38. Wireframe is now the solid surfaces with a thin black line on every edge, drawn as Triangles, Polygons or Outline.

    Run it on your own machine.
